To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mtDNA sequences retrieved from Neandertals are different from those retrieved from modern humans, that there is no evidence that mtDNA sequences similar or identical to those of Neandertals occur in early modern humans, and that there is therefore no evidence of a large contribution of mtDNA by Neandertal to early modern humans.

1) the mtDNA of all four Neandertales analyzed here is closely related to previously determined Neandertal sequences, 2) none of the five modern humans analyzed here carried Neandertal-related mtDNA sequences, and 3) these results exclude any large genetic contribution of Neandertals into modern humans.
(1) the mtDNA sequences of four Neanderts were not found among the 40 early modern humans and (2) there is no evidence that the mtDNAs of early modern humans have been contaminated by Neandertal DNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of a genetic contribution by Neanderthals to early modern man.
the question of a Neandertal genetic contribution to early modern humans.
the question of whether or not the mtDNA sequences of Neandertals are similar to those found among modern humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mtDNA sequences found in Neandertals are not found in any of the modern human populations analyzed to date.
there is no evidence of Neandertals contributing to the gene pool or to the mitochondrial gene pool of early modern humans.
the Neandertals are not the ancestors of modern humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mtDNA of Neandertals is so divergent from that of current humans that it is not detectable in current humans.
there is no evidence of Neandertals in the gene pool of early modern humans.
there is no detectable mtDNA sequence contribution of Neandertals into the mtDNA pool of early modern humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Neandertal sequences can be reliably identified among the mtDNA sequences of early modern humans.
the mtDNA sequences from the four Neandertalis are not modern contaminations.
Neandertals were not a genetically homogenous group, and that their mtDNA sequences were not identical to those of modern humans.
